name: InstaForex
lead: The only one that publishes spread, commission, swaps, and lot size without registering. And the only one whose contract size differs from all the others — an easy way to be off by a factor of ten.

items.caption: Registration form: name, email, phone, country/region (detected automatically by IP), currency, and account type (MT4/MT5).
The full specifications page shows all 5 account types at once and a spread/swap/lot table for each — worth checking before you choose.
The terms-agreement checkbox — NOT ticked by default, tick it manually.

blocks.body: After you submit the form, the confirmation page issues two passwords — a trading one and an investor one. The trading password is for logging into the terminal; the investor one gives view-only access to the account, with no right to trade.

blocks.register_note: An active company in the BVI register. The register doesn't publish the licence number itself — the link between it and this company comes only from the broker's own statement.
blocks.quote: «InstaFinance Ltd, reg. number 1811672 ... License number SIBA/L/14/1082 issued by the BVI FSC.»
blocks.confirm_note: Named right in the homepage's footer, after scrolling all the way down — the registration form itself doesn't mention the entity. Right next to it, a second group company — Insta Global Ltd, Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines — with no licence and no regulator, just a trademark holder.
missing: a compensation fund — instead of insurance, there's only a promotion tied to referring friends or a tenfold deposit
a published percentage of losing accounts

🔴 negative balance protection — the only one of the five partners without it. The contract explicitly states the opposite right: "The Company reserves the right to restore a negative balance on one of the Client's accounts using funds available on their other accounts"

blocks.title: Fees for funding methods aren't visible
blocks.body: The deposit and withdrawal pages are behind a login, so you can't compare the cost of methods before registering. This is the one thing InstaForex doesn't show publicly — everything else, it does.

blocks.title: No screenshots — requires logging into the dashboard

blocks.body: A demo account doesn't require verification: the form only asks for country, email, currency, and virtual deposit size.

blocks.title: Conditions are published in full, no registration needed
The lot here is 10,000, not 100,000
body: This is the key thing to know about InstaForex when comparing brokers. A "0.6-point" spread here isn't $6 a round turn, it's 60 cents — but the position is also ten times smaller. You can't compare spreads in points with other brokers, only through the money cost of a round turn.

Silver is 500 oz instead of the standard 5,000. And be careful: gold has two symbols with a fivefold difference in contract size — GOLD.m is 100 oz, XAUUSD.m is 500 oz. Open a position in the wrong symbol and you'll get five times the volume you expected.

blocks.title: Where crypto costs hide
blocks.body: Bitcoin's spread is 25 cents, and it's easy to stop looking there. But a 0.1% commission on volume, at a price around $64,000, works out to roughly $64 one-way and $128 for a round turn. The real cost of the trade isn't where you're looking.

blocks.title: Gold's long swap
blocks.body: −327 versus +0.69 short. Holding a gold buy position overnight here costs roughly three spreads. For anyone trading gold beyond intraday, that matters more than the spread.
